senses.def: a large boat with sails or an engine, used for pleasure or racing
ex: They sailed round the island on a yacht.
The millionaire owns a luxury yacht.

senses.def: yes (informal)
ex: 'Are you coming?' 'Yeah, I'll be there.'

senses.def: a period of twelve months, or 365 days
ex: I have lived here for three years.
Last year we went to Turkey.

senses.def: used to give someone's age
ex: She is ten years old.

mistake.note: In English you must say 'years old' when giving someone's age.

senses.def: a loud shout
ex: I heard a yell from the garden.

senses.def: to shout loudly, usually because you are angry or excited
ex: Don't yell at me!
The fans yelled with excitement.

senses.def: used to give a positive answer or to agree
ex: 'Do you like coffee?' 'Yes, I do.'
Yes, you can come in.

senses.def: until now; used in questions and negatives
ex: Have you finished yet?
I haven't seen the film yet.

senses.def: from now until the future
ex: There is no need to leave yet.

senses.def: but; in spite of that
ex: He is rich, yet he is unhappy.
The test was easy, yet many students failed.

mistake.wrong: I didn't finish yet my homework.
mistake.right: I haven't finished my homework yet.
mistake.note: Yet usually goes at the end of the clause, and is used with the present perfect.

senses.def: to produce a result, crop or profit
ex: The research yielded good results.
The trees yield a lot of fruit.

senses.def: to stop opposing something and allow it to happen
ex: The government refused to yield to the pressure.
Yield to traffic on the main road.

senses.def: a system of exercises for the body and mind that involves stretching and controlled breathing
ex: She does yoga every morning.
I joined a yoga class.

senses.def: used to talk to the person or people you are speaking or writing to
ex: Are you ready?
I'll call you tomorrow.

senses.def: used to mean people in general
ex: You can't park here.
You need a visa to enter that country.

senses.def: having lived or existed for only a short time
ex: She is a young teacher.
The children are too young to go alone.

senses.def: belonging to or connected with the person you are talking to
ex: Is this your bag?
Please open your books.

mistake.note: Your shows ownership; you're is the short form of 'you are'.

senses.def: something that belongs to the person you are talking to
ex: Is this pen yours?
My house is bigger than yours.

senses.def: used at the end of a letter before your name
ex: Yours sincerely, Anna Brown.

senses.def: used when the person you are talking to is also the object of the action
ex: Look at yourself in the mirror.
Be careful or you'll hurt yourself.

senses.def: used to emphasise 'you'
ex: Did you make this cake yourself?

senses.def: the time of life when you are young
ex: He spent his youth in a small village.
In her youth, she loved dancing.

senses.def: young people in general
ex: The youth of today use technology all the time.

senses.def: looking or behaving as if you are young
ex: He has a youthful face for his age.
She has youthful energy.

senses.def: tasting very good (informal)
ex: This chocolate cake is yummy.
What a yummy smell!
